item.title: Hong Kong, un año después del incendio: damnificados vuelven a despedir a sus seres queridos
item.description: El 25 de noviembre de 2025, un mar de llamas incineró un complejo residencial en la excolonia británica de Hong Kong. El fuego acabó con la vida de 168 personas que no pudieron escapar. Las víctimas, que lo perdieron todo, regresaron a lo que eran sus casas para despedirse de sus seres queridos fallecidos durante el incendio. El Gobierno ofreció a los damnificados un plan de recompra y apartamentos de reemplazo; aunque la mayoría aceptó la propuesta, la pérdida va más allá de lo material. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: ‘I was physically beating myself up before a take’: Rory Culkin on anxiety, fatherhood and his famous brothers
item.description: The star of Lords of Chaos, Scream 4 and Gabriel was always drawn to the dark side. Is that why he seems happier in Hollywood than his better-known brothers – and why he loved making Nocturne with Stephen Graham? Rory Culkin is enjoying the autumn afternoon in a Manhattan park. The trees are a dazzling blur of yellows, greens, oranges and reds; the background silence is so pure you can hear it. “I’m here with my baby daughter, Havoc,” he says. “Havoc Moon.” I tell him that is the spookiest name ever. “Thank you,” he says. item.title: Chemicals, Covid and cabbage: why 2026 has been an amazing year for documentaries
item.description: With Musk, NAZA and You Can See Everything finding large audiences, non-fiction cinema is poised to break through. Specifically, that time arrives each November in the form of the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA for short), with its tales of crisis and strife, angry resistance and everyday human kindness. item.title: Blade Runner 2099: fans will have no idea what is happening in this sci-fi sequel. Why is it even on TV?
item.description: If you’re a cyberpunk who loves ennui and watching actors you can’t see speak words you can’t hear, get stuck in! The rest of us will just be baffled and bored Why is James Bond not a TV series by now? Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Alien, Star Wars – all given the TV treatment. Franchise-mining is fantastic business, maximising attention share in order to sell adverts. So why not Bond, which is co-owned by Amazon? Maybe watching a punchy sex addict every week, saying his name with weirdly administrative syntax, might just be … too much? item.title: More sex, different endings: how fan fiction makes our dreams come true
item.description: From Heated Rivalry to Harry Potter, popular series are inspiring fan fiction read by thousands online. item.title: You Can See Everything passes $100m at global box office as UK release starts strong
item.description: The documentary from Nathan Fielder following fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her imprisonment has broken box office records in the UK Elizabeth Holmes film You Can See Everything has crossed the $100m mark at the global box office as it recorded the highest ever opening weekend figure for a non-music documentary in the UK. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything earned an estimated $2.5m over the weekend on its sixth week of release in North America, according to Box Office Mojo , bringing its total there to $93.5m. item.title: ‘Reminds me of home’: why Coming to America is my feelgood movie
item.description: The latest in our series of writers picking their most rewatched comfort films is an ode to Eddie Murphy’s beloved culture-clash comedy “Good morning, my neighbors!” A young Eddie Murphy shouts from the balcony of a shady apartment building.
